name: ROSS - Remote Operated Semantic Sketching
tagline: A robot that draws paintings onto a blind person's palm with warm and cold brushes, with narration.
problem: Galleries are mostly 2D visual work; blind and low-vision visitors cannot experience paintings.
solution: Segment a painting into meaningful objects, convert each into simplified stroke graphs and millimetre coordinates, and have a two-axis robot trace them on the palm; warm vs cold colours map to heated vs cooled brushes, with narration and mood music in a Bob Ross voice.
demo_moment: Photograph a painting by voice, then feel its shapes drawn on your hand while a familiar voice describes them.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Clear human stakes: a specific group gets access to culture they are excluded from.
The warm/cold two-brush feature was not working; the team demoed one brush and no colour, and still reached the finals — a working core beat a complete feature list.
Dropped an LLM-based simplification approach for a deterministic geometric pipeline after inconsistent results.
Bob Ross as name and narrator makes the accessibility message warm and memorable.
Featured by the organizer as a past showcase project.

lessons: Cut the broken feature from the demo and describe it as next; never let the unfinished part define the pitch.
When an LLM step is flaky, replace it with deterministic code before demo day.
